dossiers.subject: Uruk and early Sumerian recordkeeping

claims.text: A proto-cuneiform tablet, probably from Uruk, records quantities interpreted as barley distribution. It provides material evidence of early administrative writing; the interpretation remains qualified.

integrationNotes: Do not describe the object as the first invention of writing in a specific year.
The findspot is qualified as probable. This source does not establish a political boundary for Uruk.

dossiers.subject: Babylon in the Neo-Babylonian period

claims.text: Under Nebuchadnezzar II, Babylon's monumental building program included glazed-brick decoration at the Ishtar Gate and Processional Way, linking craft production with the city's ceremonial landscape.

evidence.locator: Nebuchadnezzar II's Babylon, Ishtar Gate and Processional Way

candidateTransitions.text: Cyrus conquered Babylon in 539 BCE. The city continued as one of the Achaemenid royal capitals.

evidence.locator: Conquest in 539 BCE and subsequent Achaemenid Babylon

integrationNotes: The existing babylonia record spans a broader interval. Do not replace it with a Neo-Babylonian identity without reviewing its features and links.
Political conquest is not the end of Babylonian cultural life. Check target geometry at the transition year before enabling a dated map jump.

integrationNotes: The card uses the existing runtime schema. Its bibliography identifies the source supporting all three subject sections.
The imported circa 1000 to 1492 polity interval has not been independently validated by this packet.
No precise founding year, collapse event, successor or kingdom polygon is inferred from the architectural evidence.

dossiers.subject: Caral-Supe

claims.text: Caral combined monumental platform structures with sunken circular courts. UNESCO reports radiocarbon evidence for its development between 3000 and 1800 BCE.

evidence.locator: Description; Integrity and Authenticity, radiocarbon paragraph

integrationNotes: A site boundary must not be presented as a kingdom's territorial extent.
Resolve the city, the wider Supe Valley settlement network and any proposed polity identity separately.

dossiers.subject: Liangzhu

claims.text: Liangzhu's archaeological remains connect a rice-based regional society with large water-management works and an organized urban landscape. Jade objects also preserve evidence of status and belief.

evidence.locator: Description and Outstanding Universal Value, water works, rice cultivation and jade

integrationNotes: The archaeological property, the distribution of Liangzhu material culture and political control require distinct geometries.
Do not assign every dam or artifact the same precise year from this broad period.

dossiers.subject: Gunditjmara knowledge and Budj Bim aquaculture

claims.text: Gunditjmara aquaculture at Budj Bim uses channels, weirs and dams to trap, store and harvest kooyang, the short-finned eel. UNESCO describes continuing knowledge and practice associated with this landscape.

evidence.locator: Description and Outstanding Universal Value, aquaculture and Gunditjmara continuity

integrationNotes: Preserve the source's relative age; do not subtract it from the current year to invent a precise construction date.
The generated gunditjmara record spans circa 1600 to 1815 and lacks an explicit culture kind. Review these fields before using them to describe the society's duration.
A continuing society should not receive an invented fell-to event. Aquaculture features do not establish a state's political frontier.
